Getting here

Bus. Route 51 stops at Miller Way and Research Way, a short walk away. Buses to Derriford Hospital also stop nearby.
Car. Please contact us before your visit if you plan to park.
Running late or lost? Email dylan.curtin@plymouth.ac.uk.

If you have any access needs, let us know before your visit and we’ll make arrangements.

title: How to take part
text:
If you’d like to take part, please read the information sheet and then complete the short online screening questionnaire. If everything is fine, we’ll be in touch to arrange your first visit.
Take the screening → Email us
If you have any questions first, email Dr Dylan Curtin at dylan.curtin@plymouth.ac.uk.
The same address is the one to use for anything about your visits, such as rescheduling, a change in your health or medication, or if you decide to withdraw.

title: How to take part
text:
Concerns or complaints
Contact the Faculty of Health Research Ethics and Integrity Committee at Research.Ethics@plymouth.ac.uk. For questions about your data, the University’s Data Protection Officer is dpo@plymouth.ac.uk.

title: Planning your visit
text: A few things to do, or avoid, before each visit. If any of these are difficult for you, please let us know.

title: Planning your visit
text:
Every visit

Get a good night’s sleep, have something to eat beforehand and come well hydrated.
Have tea or coffee as you normally would. The important thing is to keep it the same before every visit.
Bring your glasses or contact lenses if you use them.

title: Planning your visit
text:
Visit 1: The MRI scan

Wear comfortable clothes with no metal in them. Avoid “anti-odour” sportswear, which contains metal threads. A non-wired bra is best.
Take out metal jewellery and piercings. There are lockers for your belongings.
No eye make-up.
The scanner is noisy. We give you earplugs, and you’ll have a buzzer to squeeze if you want to stop.

If you think you’d find lying still in an enclosed space difficult, let us know before your visit.

title: Planning your visit
text:
Visits 2 to 4: Ultrasound and task
During these visits we put a small amount of water-based gel on part of your scalp, sticky sensors on your chest and hand, and a soft strap around your chest. Cameras track your eyes and face during the game.

Wear a loose top, ideally with layers, so we can place the chest sensors and strap easily. You won’t need to take any clothing off.
Come with clean, dry hair with no products in it.
No hand cream. We put small sensors on your fingers and cream stops them working.
No mascara, eyeliner, false lashes or lash extensions, as they affect the eye tracking.
You can wash the gel out before you leave. We have a shower, towels and shampoo, or bring your own.

title: Help us understand how the brain shapes mood and motivation
text: We’re looking for healthy adults aged 21 to 65 for a paid study at the University of Plymouth, using MRI and gentle, non-invasive brain stimulation.

title: Help us understand how the brain shapes mood and motivation
section: Why are we doing this research?
text:
Why are we doing this research?
We want to understand how deep regions of the brain shape motivation, mood and decision-making, as a first step towards more precise treatments for brain conditions. To do this, we use transcranial ultrasound. It uses sound waves, like those used in pregnancy scans, but at different settings and focused on a small area deep in the brain to gently and briefly change its activity. Read more at CENTUS.

title: Help us understand how the brain shapes mood and motivation
text:
What’s involved


At home

Online screening
15 minutes online. This is to make sure it’s safe for you to take part. Start the screening →



Visit 1

MRI scan
75 minutes. We go through the study and some extra questions with you, as well as a 30 minute scan to take pictures of your brain.



Visits 2 to 4

Ultrasound and task
90 minutes each. Up to 12 minutes of ultrasound, then a decision-making game.



At the end

£110 + up to £30 bonus
Paid at your final visit. The bonus depends on how you do in the game. You’ll also get a picture of your brain to keep.



The task. You fill a fishing net by choosing between kinds of seafood, and report how you’re feeling along the way. Sensors record your heart rate, breathing and sweat response, and cameras track your eyes and face.

title: Help us understand how the brain shapes mood and motivation
text:
Who can take part


You can take part if you’re:

aged 21 to 65
healthy, with no current or past mental health or neurological diagnosis
able to come to all four visits



You can’t take part if you:

have metal in your body
are pregnant
take certain medications
have migraines, or a personal or close family history of epilepsy
have some other health conditions



The online screening checks all of this, so if you’re not sure, get in touch. MRI and ultrasound stimulation are both non-invasive, and more than 300 people have had ultrasound stimulation at our centre. Taking part is voluntary and you can stop at any time without giving a reason. The information sheet has the full details, including how we look after your data.

title: Help us understand how the brain shapes mood and motivation
text:
How we run the study
We want our findings to apply to as many people as possible, so we aim to recruit women and men in similar numbers and welcome people of all genders. If you have access needs or anything else we should plan around, please let us know. If you have caring, work or other commitments, we’ll do our best to offer sessions outside normal working hours, although some sessions will need to take place during the working day.

title: Help us understand how the brain shapes mood and motivation
text:
The research team



The study is led by Dr Dylan Curtin in Professor Elsa Fouragnan’s lab at the Brain Research Imaging Centre, University of Plymouth. It is part of the ULTRA-GOAL project, funded by the European Union through a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions postdoctoral fellowship, and approved by the University’s Faculty of Health Research Ethics and Integrity Committee.
